learningObjective: Distinguish the semantics of AllReduce and AllGather as collective operations over a device group.

canonicalClaims.claim: AllReduce combines per-rank input tensors via an associative reduction (e.g. sum) so that every rank ends with the same reduced tensor of the input's shape; AllGather concatenates per-rank inputs along a chosen axis so that every rank ends with a tensor whose total size is N times the per-rank input.
conditions: All ranks participate with tensors of the same shape and dtype (except along the gathered axis for AllGather).
The reduction operator for AllReduce is associative (and typically commutative in practice).
nonImplications: AllReduce does not preserve per-rank identity: each rank's original contribution cannot be recovered from the output.
AllGather is not a reduction: it does no arithmetic on the payloads.

sourceMappings.locator: §2 collective operations reviewed for ML computation

misconceptions.claim: AllReduce is just AllGather followed by a local reduction on each rank, so they have identical output shape.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The output shape differs: AllReduce output matches the per-rank input shape; AllGather output is N times larger along the gathered axis. Also, ring/tree AllReduce need not materialize the full gathered tensor on any rank.

misconceptions.claim: AllGather requires the payload elements to form an associative group under some operator; otherwise it is undefined.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AllGather is a data-movement primitive with no arithmetic requirement on payloads.

misconceptions.claim: AllReduce is only defined for sum reduction; other reductions must be built as separate collectives.
misconceptions.whyWrong: AllReduce is defined for any associative reduction operator (sum, max, min, product, etc.); NCCL and MPI both support several.

implementationFacts: Ring-AllReduce is often implemented as ReduceScatter followed by AllGather, each moving (N-1)/N · S bytes per rank.
